applies_why: The judge text treats a single verse's two admitted senses as the ground for an UNDERDETERMINED label, which is what K-S2 governs.
quote: D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand": I weighed whether this forbids an UNDERDETERMINED label for a verse admitting two senses because both stand, or permits it as merely unresolved; I read it as forbidding the label.
why: The judge labels Matthew 1:16 UNDERDETERMINED precisely because a single verse admits two readings, but K-S2 says such a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand.
